title: Object Types, Interfaces, and Optional Properties
summary: Describe object shapes with interfaces and type aliases, distinguish optional properties from undefined values, and preserve excess-property checks.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply the TypeScript behavior taught in Object Types, Interfaces, and Optional Properties
Use strict compiler evidence and runtime tests to verify the contract
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Object types document required fields and their value types. Interfaces are well suited to extendable object contracts; type aliases can represent objects, unions, primitives, and tuples. `name?: string` means a property may be absent, while `name: string | undefined` requires the property key even when its value is undefined. Mark data immutable with `readonly` when mutation is not part of the contract. Fresh object literals receive excess-property checks that catch misspelled fields. Avoid broad index signatures unless every unknown key genuinely follows the same value rule.
keyPoints: Object types document required fields and their value types.
commonMistakes: a general string loses exhaustiveness checking
a type assertion is not runtime evidence

sections.heading: Guided practice
sections.content:
1. Add the example to a strict TypeScript project.
2. Predict inferred types.
3. Run `tsc --noEmit`.
4. Introduce one mismatch and read the diagnostic.
5. Correct the contract without `any`.
6. Run the JavaScript and record evidence.
